newsitem.title: UK: Large unreported copper stock unlikely - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: Large unreported copper stock unlikely - Macquarie.

text.p: "Hidden" stocks of copper in the Netherlands of up to 500,000 to 600,000 tonnes are unlikely to exist, Macquarie Equities said in their weekly commodity report.

"The report (of the stocks) is based on questionable historical statistics rather than hard evidence and we believe that the existence of such large hidden stocks is unlikely in Europe or indeed anywhere else in the world," Macquarie said.
Macquarie said copper prices have considerable upside potential in the near term, with cash values possibly hitting $1.10 to $1.20 cents per pound ($2,425 to $2,646 a tonne).
Cash copper was valued at around $2,310 early on Monday.
Macquarie said Chinese imports of copper cathode are likely to be at least 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes higher in 1996 than last year.
The report estimated total net copper cathode imports of 245,000 tonnes this year from net exports of 17,000 tonnes in 1995. In 1997 China's net imports were pegged at 220,000 tonnes.
The rise in 1996 imports reflected continued consumption growth and falling imports of copper scrap.
The reduction in availability of copper scrap in the Western world and primary copper from Russia were also bullish for the market, Macquarie added.
